title: DC-area forecast: The nicest week in months is here
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Breezes diminish a little this evening as temperatures fall into and through the 60s.

What’s next? Crisp but gorgeous tomorrow, with highs near 65. Then, sunny and dry weather through Saturday, with highs mostly in the 70s.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: The coolest night of the fall so far. Under clear skies and with diminishing winds from the northwest, lows range from near 40 in our colder spots to near 50 downtown. Confidence: High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Tuesday): Fans of sunny, sweater weather will love it. After morning 40s, sunshine pushes afternoon highs into the mid-60s, with a gentle breeze from the northwest. Confidence: High 😎 Nice Day!

Tomorrow night: Clear, calm and, in some areas, cold. Lows range from the upper 30s in our coldest spots to the upper 40s downtown. Confidence: High

❤️ How to support Capital Weather

Help sustain an independent Capital Weather by becoming a free or paid supporter. Learn more at capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

The stretch from Wednesday to Saturday is simply sublime. Each day brings mostly sunny skies and highs in the 70s. Thursday is probably the warmest day of the bunch, when the warmest spots could flirt with 80. Otherwise, highs are mostly in the low to mid-70s, with nighttime lows mostly in the 50s. Confidence: Medium-High

Sunday may end up being nice, too, but it’s also possible rain could arrive at some point during the day or at night as a storm system potentially approaches from the south. Regardless, highs will probably end up pretty close to 70. Confidence: Low-Medium

DC weather history for October 5

Early flakes in the 1800s marked some of the region’s first hints of winter, while in 1995 the remnants of Hurricane Opal spawned multiple tornadoes that damaged dozens of homes across the area.

Today’s daily digit — 7/10: After morning clouds burn off, a “sun”-sational 70-degree afternoon. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
